purpose: SIDEQUEST. Two spec loops the operator asked for on 2026-09-07, run apart from the daily FILL/DECIDE/FIX cycle in a dedicated worktree so neither can touch the other. (1) AgentWeave where MCP is blocked and GitHub Copilot is the house CLI. (2) What is actually separable from this repo into standalone projects, with a folder per surviving candidate in the parent directory and a spec loop inside each. This window writes proposals and, only at the very end and only if time remains, one prototype skeleton. It does NOT implement anything in AgentWeave.
playbook: none -- this is a one-off run, not a recurring window. The queue below is the whole instruction. Round discipline is CLAUDE.md's.

queue.title: Spec loop R1 -- AgentWeave reachable where MCP is blocked
queue.detail: Read openspec/explorations/2026-09-07-agentweave-without-mcp-and-with-copilot.md FIRST. It is a seed, not a proposal: it carries measurements to re-check and a list of questions you must ANSWER rather than inherit, and it contains one deliberately-flagged false claim to remind you the base rate is not zero. Answer its question 1 before writing anything -- is this one change or two? The default assumption is two, HTTP path first, because the HTTP path is what makes a Copilot runner worth having and because the non-MCP branch telling an agent it has no tools (launchability.py:325-330) is a live defect for ANY harness without MCP. Write the proposal into openspec/changes/<name>/ with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and the specs/<capability>/ delta. `openspec validate --strict <name>` must pass; SHALL goes on line 1 of a requirement. Note that agent-capability-plane/spec.md:107-118 already REQUIRES this parity and names the forbidden-MCP case -- so check whether this is a new requirement or an unbuilt shipped one, because that changes whether the delta is ADDED or MODIFIED.
queue.result: Wrote openspec/changes/2026-09-07-an-agent-without-mcp-is-not-told-it-has-nothing/ (proposal, design, tasks, agent-capability-plane delta). `openspec validate --strict` passes. Answered seed question 1: TWO changes, HTTP first. Delta is ADDED (a run without MCP is told how to reach the plane) + MODIFIED (the shipped parity requirement, which is currently breached). Two findings beyond the seed: (1) route parity is not behaviour parity -- ask_user's blocking, ordering, declined-vs-expired and wait-ended report all live in mcp_server.py:306-472, not in the three routes; (2) archive_job's always-confirm rule (mcp_server.py:815, design D18) is absent from POST /jobs/{job_id}/archive, and test_agent_actions_governed.py:137-140 asserts 200 for the unconfirmed HTTP archive under a comment stating the opposite rule -- a live disagreement with one side green. One seed gap LEFT the change: _decide (mcp_server.py:901-953) guards the harness's own tools via --permission-prompt-tool and explicitly allows mcp__agentweave__* outright, so it is not a capability-plane boundary; it moves to the Copilot change as a stated obligation.

Check the claim that is easiest to get wrong: the 26-tool HTTP mapping is a claim about ROUTES, not about whether a route behaves identically when reached without a run credential. Start with ask_user -- a blocking call is the one whose HTTP form is least likely to be equivalent. Fix the proposal where the code disagrees; if R1's argument survives unchanged, say so plainly, because a round that finds nothing is a real outcome.

queue.title: Spec loop R3 -- re-derive again, independently, and measure what can be measured
queue.detail: Third independent pass. This repo's rounds check the argument; only a drive checks the product -- and this window may not start a Hub (see limits), so say plainly what is unmeasurable here rather than asserting it. The two things most likely to be wrong and cheapest to establish without a Hub: (a) whether every mutating agent-facing route really depends on the run-credential dependency rather than the older project-key one, and (b) what happens to the permission boundary in mcp_server._decide (:901-953) for an agent with no MCP -- if it simply vanishes, the proposal must say so in design.md rather than shipping a silently weaker adapter.
queue.result: Third independent pass. Target (a) CONFIRMED and it sharpens the premise: get_agent_actor (agent_auth.py:40-80) accepts only an `aw_run_`-prefixed credential hashing to a Run with status=='running' and a matching instance id -- an operator `aw_live_` key fails on the prefix; all 32 agent_actions routes carry it (parsed, 0 without), no other module imports it, and a scan of every mutating decorator under hub/hub/api/v1/ found none without an auth dependency. Neither earlier round said the sharpest part: _hub_request (mcp_server.py:151-183) authenticates with os.environ['AW_RUN_TOKEN'] against os.environ['HUB_URL']+'/api/v1/agent-actions', so the MCP adapter IS a wrapper over the two variables the notice tells the agent it has nothing to do with. Target (b) did NOT hold and changed the design: mcp_command is set iff access_path=='mcp' (agent_trigger.py:1025-1028) and the approver is itself an MCP tool, so the access path decides the run's PERMISSION POSTURE too. MEASURED via build_command (pure function, no Hub): 'mcp' -> --mcp-config + --allowedTools + --permission-prompt-tool + --permission-mode manual; 'cli' -> no approver and --permission-mode acceptEdits, which the repo's own comment (runner_commands.py:66-67) calls WIDER than workspace. So design D1's claim that the notice and the boundary are unrelated is wrong -- they share a variable, and each of D7's three mechanisms moves containment as a side effect of deciding what a run is told. Delta gains one scenario ('A truer description does not silently widen permission'); design gains D9 and D10; tasks gain 4.7-4.9. Mirror severity raised: in the operator's deployment the Hub emits --permission-prompt-tool naming an MCP tool the harness cannot provide, and runner_commands.py:245-248 predicts every tool call then fails -- labelled unverified, moved into the drive (6.5). Two corrections to R2: (1) restoring the probe is self-defeating -- probe_mcp_registered shells a SEPARATE `<cli> mcp list` with no --mcp-config, so it cannot see the per-invocation injected server, would answer False for every injected run and thereby remove the injection it was asked about; (2) three test files shaped by the removed probe, not two -- test_launchability.py:390-429's TestAccessPath class has a false docstring and two more F190-shaped tests. R2's own resolve_access_path measurement re-ran and reproduced exactly. openspec validate --strict passes; no product code touched.
